cards.text: Meet Saul. Last time he showed up, he was dragging off men and women and putting them in prison (Acts 8:3). Now he's still breathing out murderous threats against the disciples of the Lord, and friend, that's not a bad mood, that's a LIFESTYLE.

cards.question: Saul wants to go after the disciples of the Lord. Who does he go to see first?

cards.text: Saul asks the high priest for letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so he can go after the Way there. Friend, this man isn't just mad, he's got PAPERWORK.

cards.question: True or false: Saul's plan in Damascus is to go after only the men who belong to the Way.
Saul wants to bring the believers he finds in Damascus back as prisoners to ___.

cards.text: So Saul hits the road with his letters. He's almost to Damascus when suddenly a light from heaven flashes around him.

cards.question: A light from heaven just flashed around Saul on the road. What happens to him?

answers.text: He hides his face in his cloak

cards.text: Then he hears a voice say to him, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?” Friend, when somebody says your name TWICE, you already know it's serious.

cards.question: Saul answers the voice, “Who are You, Lord?” Who is speaking to him?

cards.text: “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,” He replied. Saul's been chasing down believers, and the whole time he's been chasing JESUS.

cards.question: True or false: Right there on the road, Jesus tells Saul everything he must do.

cards.text: Not yet. Jesus says, “Now get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do.”

cards.question: Saul isn't traveling alone. While all this happens, the men with him stand there ___.
True or false: The men traveling with Saul hear the voice but don't see anyone.

cards.text: Saul gets up from the ground, but when he opens his eyes, he can't see a thing. Friend, the man carrying the high priest's letters can't even READ them now.

cards.question: Saul can't see a thing. How do the men traveling with him get him into Damascus?
For ___ days Saul is without sight, and he doesn't eat or drink anything.

cards.text: In Damascus there's a disciple named Ananias, and the Lord speaks to him in a vision. “Here I am, Lord,” Ananias answers.
The Lord tells him to go to the house of a man named Judas on Straight Street. Friend, the Lord gives better directions than my phone ever has.

cards.question: The Lord sends Ananias to that house on Straight Street. Who is he supposed to ask for there?

answers.text: A man from Tarsus named Saul
A man from Cyprus named Barnabas
A man from Cyrene named Simon

cards.question: The Lord tells Ananias that Saul is praying, and that Saul has seen a vision too. What does Saul see in it?

cards.text: Ananias pushes back. He tells the Lord many people have told him about this man and all the harm he has done to the Lord's saints in Jerusalem.

cards.question: True or false: Ananias also tells the Lord that Saul has come to Damascus with authority from the chief priests to arrest all who call on His name.

cards.text: “Go!” said the Lord. I bet Ananias's knees were knocking louder than his hand was about to knock on that door.

cards.question: The Lord calls Saul His chosen instrument to carry His name. Who will Saul carry it to?

cards.text: The Gentiles and their kings, and the people of Israel. From arrest letters to KINGS, friend, that's not a promotion, that's a whole new LIFE.

cards.question: True or false: The Lord says Saul's work for His name will come without any suffering.

cards.text: The Lord says, “I will show him how much he must suffer for My name.” So Ananias goes to the house and places his hands on Saul.

cards.question: Ananias places his hands on Saul and greets him as ___ Saul.

cards.text: He says the Lord Jesus, who appeared to Saul on the road, sent him so Saul may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit. The man Ananias just warned the Lord about is now BROTHER Saul.

cards.question: Ananias has his hands on Saul and has just told him why the Lord sent him. What happens to Saul at that instant?

answers.text: He sees a vision of heaven

cards.question: True or false: Once his sight is restored, Saul gets up and is baptized.

cards.text: Saul takes some food and gets his strength back, and after three days of nothing, I believe it. Friend, I get cranky if I skip ONE cookie.

cards.question: Saul's strength is back. He spends the next several days in Damascus with the ___.

cards.text: And trust me, friend, the oven's still on, because Saul's story is just getting started.

findings.problem: Stop 1 overuses unrevealed-detail guesses. Cards 2, 5, 7, 11, 14 and 17 do not provide enough earlier context to eliminate the alternatives, making six of the stop's ten choices discovery guesses rather than informed ones. Rework several setups or questions so only a few discoveries remain.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The correct answer stands out visually: "Jesus" is a bare one-word answer, while both wrong answers are three-word descriptions, "The angel Gabriel" and "The prophet Elijah." Make the answers comparable in length and form.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: "While all this happens" depends on earlier cards without identifying what the men are reacting to. The question should briefly reestablish the light-and-voice encounter so it remains self-contained when the story card is no longer visible.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: "That house" points back to story card 2, which is no longer on screen. Identify it in the question as the house of Judas on Straight Street.
